answer: Each agent registers on a ferrous‑signed ledger that issues a cryptographic signal tied to a verifiable stake; new identities receive a jetty‑level weight that grows only as the square of their accrued stake. When consensus forms, votes are multiplied by the square of the weight, so a thousand Sybil nodes count as one well‑staked agent. An attacker must invest quadratically more resources, making a cheap identity flood economically prohibitive.
